orig_text:
During the Control phase, the sender SHALL read the current system
   (wall-clock) time and populate the authUnixTime field and next
   calculate the 32-octet HMAC-SHA-256 hash of the entire PDU according
   to Section 6 of [RFC6234] (with the authDigest and checkSum preset to
   all zeroes).  The authDigest field is filled by the result, then the
   packet is sent to the receiver.  The value in the authUnixTime field
   is a 32-bit timestamp, and a 10-second tolerance window (+/- 5
   seconds) SHALL be used by the receiver to distinguish a subsequent
   replay of a PDU.  See Table 2 of [TR-471] for a recommended timestamp
   resolution.
correct_text:
During the Control phase, the sender SHALL read the current system
   (wall-clock) time and populate the authUnixTime field and next
   calculate the 32-octet HMAC-SHA-256 hash of the entire PDU according
   to Section 6 of [RFC6234] (with the authDigest and checkSum preset to
   all zeroes).  The authDigest field is filled by the result, then the
   packet is sent to the receiver.  The value in the authUnixTime field
   is a 32-bit timestamp, and a 10-second tolerance window (+/- 5
   seconds) SHALL be used by the receiver to enforce PDU immediacy and
   accommodate clock skew.  See Table 2 of [TR-471] for a recommended
   timestamp resolution.

   Because a +/- 5-second tolerance window alone cannot distinguish or
   prevent replays of an authentic PDU arriving within that 10-second
   window, and because Section 5.4.1 derives the test-connection key
   solely from (Kin, "UDPSTP", client Setup authUnixTime), receivers
   MUST track recently accepted Test Setup Request PDUs (for example, by
   caching (keyId, authUnixTime, authDigest) across the full tolerance
   window) to detect replays and MUST NOT allocate new test sessions or
   ephemeral test ports for replayed Setup Requests.  To prevent two
   legitimate tests under the same keyId from sharing a derived session
   key, clients SHOULD avoid reusing the same authUnixTime value across
   Setup Requests.  Furthermore, because controlHdrTA (Section 7.1) does
   not carry testPort or the Setup authUnixTime, receivers MUST bind each
   derived key strictly to the single test connection's 4-tuple (client
   address/port and assigned server testPort) and reject duplicate
   (authUnixTime, authDigest) pairs within a connection.
notes:
Methodology & Tooling Disclosure:
I am not claiming personal expertise at the level of formal protocol verification; this submission was heavily assisted by Google Gemini alongside my open-source RFC-LLM pipeline (https://github.com/mariobx/RFC-LLM) and MITRE CPSA 4.4.9 (`cpsa4`). All RFC quotes were verified verbatim against rfc9946.txt, the counterexamples were produced mechanically by `cpsa4`, and three behaviors were dynamically reproduced on localhost against compiled BroadbandForum/obudpst v9.1.0 (git ceb8917): (1) replaying one captured Setup Request within the tolerance window created additional sessions on new ephemeral testPorts, (2) those sessions derived identical session keys because the HKDF context contains only the client Setup authUnixTime, and (3) a captured TESTACTUS PDU sent from a different source IP/port to a replayed session testPort was accepted, submitted in good faith for WG / Area Director review.


Section 5.3.1 currently asserts that "a 10-second tolerance window (+/- 5 seconds) SHALL be used by the receiver to distinguish a subsequent replay of a PDU." A wall-clock tolerance window only rejects stale PDUs older than 5 seconds; it provides zero replay detection within the 10-second acceptance window.

In RFC 9946, this deficiency interacts with two additional design omissions:

1. Key Derivation Function Context (Section 5.4.1 and Appendix A):
   The HKDF-HMAC-SHA256 key derivation uses only:
     - Kin: shared key identified by keyId
     - Label: "UDPSTP"
     - Context: UTF-8 string of the client's initial Setup Request authUnixTime
   Neither the server's Setup Response authUnixTime, the server-assigned ephemeral testPort, a high-entropy nonce, nor client/server endpoint identifiers appear in Context.

2. Test Activation PDU Binding (Section 7.1, controlHdrTA):
   The Test Activation PDU header (controlHdrTA) covers pduId, protocolVer, cmdRequest, cmdResponse, test parameters, authMode, authUnixTime, authDigest, keyId, and checkSum, but omits testPort, mcIdent, mcIndex, and the initial Setup authUnixTime.

Consequences:
- An attacker who captures an authentic authenticated Setup Request (CHSR_CREQ_SETUPREQ) can replay it to the server multiple times within the 10-second (+/- 5 s) window.
- Without Setup Request replay deduplication, each replayed Setup Request causes the server to spawn a new test session (bypassing or exhausting Section 11 item 4's simultaneous-test limit) on a new ephemeral testPort while deriving the EXACT SAME session key from the repeated client Setup authUnixTime.
- Similarly, if an honest client opens two tests within the same 1-second authUnixTime tick under the same keyId, both sessions share identical derived keys and an attacker can splice or replay TESTACTUS (controlHdrTA) messages across connections/testPorts whenever source-tuple validation is loose or shared behind NAT.

Formal Verification Evidence:
Automated cryptographic protocol analysis using MITRE CPSA 4.4.9 (cpsa4) finds, in a model of RFC 9946 written by the pipeline from the RFC text (udpstp.scm / udpstp_shapes.txt, realized shapes label 12 and label 22), both Setup Request replay and cross-session Test Activation key collision/parameter disagreement: two distinct Server responder strands accept the exact same CHSR_CREQ_SETUPREQ message, emit distinct Setup Responses (different setup_response_fields and setup_response_auth_unix_time), derive the same session key from (shared_key, "UDPSTP", setup_auth_unix_time), and accept the same CHTA_CREQ_TESTACTUS message. This is a result about the model, not a machine-checked proof about RFC 9946 itself.

Supporting model artifacts:
- CPSA model:
  https://github.com/mariobx/Errata-for-RFC-Editor/blob/main/RFC9946/udpstp.scm
- Non-shapes XHTML output:
  https://github.com/mariobx/Errata-for-RFC-Editor/blob/main/RFC9946/udpstp.xhtml
- Shapes XHTML output:
  https://github.com/mariobx/Errata-for-RFC-Editor/blob/main/RFC9946/udpstp_shapes.xhtml

Independent of the model, the three behaviors above were observed on localhost against the compiled obudpst v9.1.0 server.

Scope Note per IESG Errata Processing Guidelines (May 2021):
Changing the Section 5.4.1 HKDF Context (to include a server nonce, client nonce, and testPort) or extending controlHdrTA (Section 7.1) to authenticate testPort and the Setup session identifier changes the wire protocol and must be done in a future -bis specification. The Corrected Text above corrects the inaccurate timestamp-window claim in Section 5.3.1 and specifies wire-compatible replay caching and 4-tuple session isolation.
